A liver enzyme blood test (often part of a liver panel or comprehensive metabolic panel) `measures specific enzymes and proteins in your blood to check for liver inflammation, injury, or bile duct issues` . Elevated levels do not automatically diagnose a specific disease, so doctors interpret them alongside your symptoms, risk factors, and follow-up tests.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkAEBxCJF10G_Qfd1fkhE32kO60qXyogmDkMR2gLShQP8pELkVQHeXQPbVaFBFxSDgwiktLjb7UnpJj4JdkXe-pTyEJVwqJdDBn3XUFfNLukPuvo4W41GbgpOze4bDECkQDzVyNjoU_yuxM0J6nhLmEe54lj3DehuVMW8cc0IxwAL1D8-koWlDKzvvTRlvv7SWQs)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdAHEIkXXYuRTnKaFawim3edqX8Vjbe6pTHNfX302C1xT-olGbRszBmBIqjsEkX_KONhxYI_o7FwQEf8BExFGGN3IIfjrgtKFscPRhlM3Ru5OaZvPUcQwW2y0kAT_2VVpb7BduDtWV2zlBQJ3SRkqEbiunaiO)[[3]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FmdjZrnEEu4&t=5)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESiQEBxCJF159zb8zs63B_1POPm3uDn4M8gy1AlU6H900dz9JAyysovc0XCEFulzb_502abmhkPk5lgAaUnrT36PD_qTeo1N2Ibe9BnczutC7Wm5_KMb_t4uU7JT76VnM4jKzkx5Hgk2Wxh-nTJxODUoWJRP4NF55sv9VuYoShrzgXVxc9OJaGKbSnyg)

### Key Enzymes Tested

- **ALT (Alanine transaminase):** Found mostly in the liver. High levels often point to liver cell stress or injury.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESiQEBxCJF159zb8zs63B_1POPm3uDn4M8gy1AlU6H900dz9JAyysovc0XCEFulzb_502abmhkPk5lgAaUnrT36PD_qTeo1N2Ibe9BnczutC7Wm5_KMb_t4uU7JT76VnM4jKzkx5Hgk2Wxh-nTJxODUoWJRP4NF55sv9VuYoShrzgXVxc9OJaGKbSnyg)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESlAEBxCJF189Kf5JGE3ZmA3q1WhIhS4YEv7Pk8IlVfKvGoQUtMxTIpfGlv9ezuZey-2IsmMlkhmOFbbVQ3h2o-WVUGmwl9wIDMaUnLZ7_AOiWME8l3Sjp6rXqHlaJAs_g0-nLNRqctTTcAnWeKdbieoiHX-2tOKfO_mHrCPEGX7QL7e7ddAkTtP16YIxJ2Bn6h4DgNKcf)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbQHEIkXXuE2rbwbaC5UFZLrZ976XCWFJCkytMr7R52WEdoHxLnChcEDLXSHgQf6SWP1Eo7DOnHDa3WotUEGkI_A6sKq_W7s0gMs7EQXHMkNxVsNpB6hzalPXOC8M4XLek0K9GPBeOJdqSSxq-M4)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESiAEBxCJF1_WJ38KD-bGiAXV0db7_llwDE1-XfDLXhz6xg2Si5GGgoHEUaFmqzOftBqwhNh5xMPj_rPWqS2q8SuIvuIWQCnMRfX3a2rHdvdHHhhzr5dNvhB6hhuli8qS4o0HgEQ8WWYG1Zakhme6O2bbZaKGCuNb8f5x5J__xTrLOBsjMGnd_56RJ)
- **AST (Aspartate aminotransferase):** Found in the liver, heart, muscles, and other tissues. High levels can signal liver or muscle injury.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESlAEBxCJF189Kf5JGE3ZmA3q1WhIhS4YEv7Pk8IlVfKvGoQUtMxTIpfGlv9ezuZey-2IsmMlkhmOFbbVQ3h2o-WVUGmwl9wIDMaUnLZ7_AOiWME8l3Sjp6rXqHlaJAs_g0-nLNRqctTTcAnWeKdbieoiHX-2tOKfO_mHrCPEGX7QL7e7ddAkTtP16YIxJ2Bn6h4DgNKcf)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbQHEIkXXuE2rbwbaC5UFZLrZ976XCWFJCkytMr7R52WEdoHxLnChcEDLXSHgQf6SWP1Eo7DOnHDa3WotUEGkI_A6sKq_W7s0gMs7EQXHMkNxVsNpB6hzalPXOC8M4XLek0K9GPBeOJdqSSxq-M4)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkAEBxCJF10G_Qfd1fkhE32kO60qXyogmDkMR2gLShQP8pELkVQHeXQPbVaFBFxSDgwiktLjb7UnpJj4JdkXe-pTyEJVwqJdDBn3XUFfNLukPuvo4W41GbgpOze4bDECkQDzVyNjoU_yuxM0J6nhLmEe54lj3DehuVMW8cc0IxwAL1D8-koWlDKzvvTRlvv7SWQs)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESiQEBxCJF159zb8zs63B_1POPm3uDn4M8gy1AlU6H900dz9JAyysovc0XCEFulzb_502abmhkPk5lgAaUnrT36PD_qTeo1N2Ibe9BnczutC7Wm5_KMb_t4uU7JT76VnM4jKzkx5Hgk2Wxh-nTJxODUoWJRP4NF55sv9VuYoShrzgXVxc9OJaGKbSnyg)
- **ALP (Alkaline phosphatase):** Found mainly in the liver, bile ducts, and bones. Elevated levels may point to bile duct blockages, liver issues, or bone activity.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESiAEBxCJF1_WJ38KD-bGiAXV0db7_llwDE1-XfDLXhz6xg2Si5GGgoHEUaFmqzOftBqwhNh5xMPj_rPWqS2q8SuIvuIWQCnMRfX3a2rHdvdHHhhzr5dNvhB6hhuli8qS4o0HgEQ8WWYG1Zakhme6O2bbZaKGCuNb8f5x5J__xTrLOBsjMGnd_56RJ)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESlAEBxCJF189Kf5JGE3ZmA3q1WhIhS4YEv7Pk8IlVfKvGoQUtMxTIpfGlv9ezuZey-2IsmMlkhmOFbbVQ3h2o-WVUGmwl9wIDMaUnLZ7_AOiWME8l3Sjp6rXqHlaJAs_g0-nLNRqctTTcAnWeKdbieoiHX-2tOKfO_mHrCPEGX7QL7e7ddAkTtP16YIxJ2Bn6h4DgNKcf)
- **GGT (Gamma-glutamyl transferase):** Found in the liver, bile ducts, and pancreas. Often checked with ALP to help confirm bile duct or liver issues, and can rise with heavy alcohol use.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESfQHEIkXX6fDIJ2JtS2S9XqRPIqnpszMx5GUBTBBdm2AJuT9TDpj6ekupByXjdsS3FaTR9YVNGMa1WP_WeDQ4IlvpR8TVWtpTO4k3dKlRUUqhyDGOT0k-wtYkZrvMUKWLPvO1n2vP1fH1OdNFi02MpwPI0JaUAJ_loPBQIp5q)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESlAEBxCJF189Kf5JGE3ZmA3q1WhIhS4YEv7Pk8IlVfKvGoQUtMxTIpfGlv9ezuZey-2IsmMlkhmOFbbVQ3h2o-WVUGmwl9wIDMaUnLZ7_AOiWME8l3Sjp6rXqHlaJAs_g0-nLNRqctTTcAnWeKdbieoiHX-2tOKfO_mHrCPEGX7QL7e7ddAkTtP16YIxJ2Bn6h4DgNKcf)[[3]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FmdjZrnEEu4&t=5)

### Related Liver Panel Markers

- **Bilirubin:** A waste product processed by the liver and excreted in bile. High levels can cause yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice).
- **Albumin & Total protein:** Proteins made by the liver. Low levels can reflect reduced liver function or other conditions.
- **PT / INR (Prothrombin time):** Measures how fast blood clots, which depends on clotting factors made by the liver.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdAHEIkXXYuRTnKaFawim3edqX8Vjbe6pTHNfX302C1xT-olGbRszBmBIqjsEkX_KONhxYI_o7FwQEf8BExFGGN3IIfjrgtKFscPRhlM3Ru5OaZvPUcQwW2y0kAT_2VVpb7BduDtWV2zlBQJ3SRkqEbiunaiO)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESlAEBxCJF189Kf5JGE3ZmA3q1WhIhS4YEv7Pk8IlVfKvGoQUtMxTIpfGlv9ezuZey-2IsmMlkhmOFbbVQ3h2o-WVUGmwl9wIDMaUnLZ7_AOiWME8l3Sjp6rXqHlaJAs_g0-nLNRqctTTcAnWeKdbieoiHX-2tOKfO_mHrCPEGX7QL7e7ddAkTtP16YIxJ2Bn6h4DgNKcf)[[3]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FmdjZrnEEu4&t=5)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESiQEBxCJF159zb8zs63B_1POPm3uDn4M8gy1AlU6H900dz9JAyysovc0XCEFulzb_502abmhkPk5lgAaUnrT36PD_qTeo1N2Ibe9BnczutC7Wm5_KMb_t4uU7JT76VnM4jKzkx5Hgk2Wxh-nTJxODUoWJRP4NF55sv9VuYoShrzgXVxc9OJaGKbSnyg)[[5]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=i2PfjEks4GQ&t=3)

### Common Reasons & Next Steps
Doctors often order this test during routine checkups, to monitor medications or existing liver conditions, or if someone has risk factors (such as alcohol use, metabolic conditions, or viral hepatitis) or symptoms like fatigue, nausea, abdominal pain, or jaundice.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESiAEBxCJF1zVGbE_RL8_ThZx7ragoR_Q14PLlqsins-RgrpD6ZT6tZA319CFKFfoSSsYfcClaRjqjPEIprhTJP06YGyvhMb86NoimMCCERss7mbtvZ4LSa27-Swj3RPV0WAO9rwX0gLdYcAfmgfBrwj_gdsn-TKvkQaTZe6dU7vRDmy5wFaHkEny3)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkAEBxCJF10G_Qfd1fkhE32kO60qXyogmDkMR2gLShQP8pELkVQHeXQPbVaFBFxSDgwiktLjb7UnpJj4JdkXe-pTyEJVwqJdDBn3XUFfNLukPuvo4W41GbgpOze4bDECkQDzVyNjoU_yuxM0J6nhLmEe54lj3DehuVMW8cc0IxwAL1D8-koWlDKzvvTRlvv7SWQs)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdAHEIkXXYuRTnKaFawim3edqX8Vjbe6pTHNfX302C1xT-olGbRszBmBIqjsEkX_KONhxYI_o7FwQEf8BExFGGN3IIfjrgtKFscPRhlM3Ru5OaZvPUcQwW2y0kAT_2VVpb7BduDtWV2zlBQJ3SRkqEbiunaiO)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbQHEIkXXuE2rbwbaC5UFZLrZ976XCWFJCkytMr7R52WEdoHxLnChcEDLXSHgQf6SWP1Eo7DOnHDa3WotUEGkI_A6sKq_W7s0gMs7EQXHMkNxVsNpB6hzalPXOC8M4XLek0K9GPBeOJdqSSxq-M4)Because temporary factors—such as certain medications, supplements, alcohol, or intense exercise—can raise enzyme levels, doctors frequently repeat the test or order imaging and targeted blood work before making a diagnosis. For more details on how results are evaluated, see [Mayo Clinic](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkAEBxCJF10G_Qfd1fkhE32kO60qXyogmDkMR2gLShQP8pELkVQHeXQPbVaFBFxSDgwiktLjb7UnpJj4JdkXe-pTyEJVwqJdDBn3XUFfNLukPuvo4W41GbgpOze4bDECkQDzVyNjoU_yuxM0J6nhLmEe54lj3DehuVMW8cc0IxwAL1D8-koWlDKzvvTRlvv7SWQs), [Cleveland Clinic](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESiQEBxCJF159zb8zs63B_1POPm3uDn4M8gy1AlU6H900dz9JAyysovc0XCEFulzb_502abmhkPk5lgAaUnrT36PD_qTeo1N2Ibe9BnczutC7Wm5_KMb_t4uU7JT76VnM4jKzkx5Hgk2Wxh-nTJxODUoWJRP4NF55sv9VuYoShrzgXVxc9OJaGKbSnyg) , and [MedlinePlus](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdAHEIkXXYuRTnKaFawim3edqX8Vjbe6pTHNfX302C1xT-olGbRszBmBIqjsEkX_KONhxYI_o7FwQEf8BExFGGN3IIfjrgtKFscPRhlM3Ru5OaZvPUcQwW2y0kAT_2VVpb7BduDtWV2zlBQJ3SRkqEbiunaiO).[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESiQEBxCJF159zb8zs63B_1POPm3uDn4M8gy1AlU6H900dz9JAyysovc0XCEFulzb_502abmhkPk5lgAaUnrT36PD_qTeo1N2Ibe9BnczutC7Wm5_KMb_t4uU7JT76VnM4jKzkx5Hgk2Wxh-nTJxODUoWJRP4NF55sv9VuYoShrzgXVxc9OJaGKbSnyg)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESiAEBxCJF1zVGbE_RL8_ThZx7ragoR_Q14PLlqsins-RgrpD6ZT6tZA319CFKFfoSSsYfcClaRjqjPEIprhTJP06YGyvhMb86NoimMCCERss7mbtvZ4LSa27-Swj3RPV0WAO9rwX0gLdYcAfmgfBrwj_gdsn-TKvkQaTZe6dU7vRDmy5wFaHkEny3)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbQHEIkXXuE2rbwbaC5UFZLrZ976XCWFJCkytMr7R52WEdoHxLnChcEDLXSHgQf6SWP1Eo7DOnHDa3WotUEGkI_A6sKq_W7s0gMs7EQXHMkNxVsNpB6hzalPXOC8M4XLek0K9GPBeOJdqSSxq-M4)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkAEBxCJF10G_Qfd1fkhE32kO60qXyogmDkMR2gLShQP8pELkVQHeXQPbVaFBFxSDgwiktLjb7UnpJj4JdkXe-pTyEJVwqJdDBn3XUFfNLukPuvo4W41GbgpOze4bDECkQDzVyNjoU_yuxM0J6nhLmEe54lj3DehuVMW8cc0IxwAL1D8-koWlDKzvvTRlvv7SWQs)[[5]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdAHEIkXXYuRTnKaFawim3edqX8Vjbe6pTHNfX302C1xT-olGbRszBmBIqjsEkX_KONhxYI_o7FwQEf8BExFGGN3IIfjrgtKFscPRhlM3Ru5OaZvPUcQwW2y0kAT_2VVpb7BduDtWV2zlBQJ3SRkqEbiunaiO)Are you looking to **interpret specific test results**, **prepare for an upcoming blood draw** , or **understand potential causes** of elevated enzymes? PT / INR (Prothrombin time): Measures how fast blood clots, which depends on clotting factors made by the liver.
